reviewed_by: Claude Code, fixing the production chat_goals revision conflicts that failed goal turns
reason: Goal turns with running subagents failed with 'revision conflict on chat_goals <id>: expected N, found N+1'. ChatService._charge_goal read the goal and wrote its usage against that revision with no retry; a subagent's usage charge (or active-time settle) committed in between, the RevisionConflict escaped _add_usage, and _stream_tool_turn saved it as the turn's error. The charge now plans the debit on the newest goal through revise_latest. Selected: the goal revision-race tests and the routed tool-turn tests (both new cases fail on main with the production message), plus the goal and subagent-lifecycle suites that charge goals.
exclusions: No UI, API shape or settings change. test_chat.py, test_provider_cost_rates.py and test_butler_resources.py goal/charge cases passed locally (26) and are not selected. The in-transaction charge path is unchanged in behaviour; a PostgreSQL check against a scratch database showed it does not conflict with its own unit's goal write. No disposable LAN Core run: the race needs concurrent subagent provider responses inside a millisecond window and is not reproducible on demand through the UI; the deterministic window tests drive the real store and the real tool-turn loop.
